document_title: VC Wavelength Router — Service Handbook SH-WR, edition 3

datasheet.value: fully flexible wavelength router (colourless, directionless and contentionless)
Each direction of the router has its own selector module.

result: The router steers every wavelength on its own.

applies_to: all the light entering on one direction
when: A problem hits all the light entering on one direction
result: the problem reappears, after the router, on each wavelength steered onwards from it

when: as long as its attenuation range allows
result: brings the wavelength levels back to the launch level

when: A drop in level of up to about 8 dB before the router
result: is evened out at the router
the noise penalty the drop caused does not go away
leaves the router as a weak wavelength
crosses the router as it arrived

faults.name: Over-attenuation
faults.description: The selector module attenuates one wavelength more than it should, so that wavelength leaves the router weak.

faults.name: Passband misalignment
faults.description: The selector module's passband for one wavelength has moved off centre or become too narrow. The wavelength's level is fine but its quality suffers.

faults.name: Direction input fault
applies_to: an input of a selector module
faults.description: An input of a selector module dies. All the light coming in on that direction stops at the router, while light entering on the other directions carries on.

effects.scope: All the light coming in on that direction
light entering on the other directions

routing: The router steers every wavelength on its own as it leaves a direction.
troubleshooting_notes: The router has no alarms for the faults below. They are seen in the spectrum monitor's readings and in the alarms of the terminals further along.
A single wavelength whose level jumps in the spectrum monitor readings is at fault at the first router where the jump is seen.
An input fault is at the input of the direction it hits; a single-wavelength fault is on that wavelength at that input.
